lead.headline: Citadel Securities marks Crypto.com at $20B as institutional market makers price in permanent crypto infrastructure
lead.tldr: Wall Street's most sophisticated market maker just placed a $20 billion valuation on a retail crypto exchange, while prediction markets, tokenization sandboxes, and regulated M&A in Singapore all point to the same repricing: crypto infrastructure is being underwritten as durable plumbing, not speculative optionality.

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, today the signals converge on a single underwriting question—whether the infrastructure being built now justifies the valuations being placed on it by operators who have no incentive to be wrong.

top_signals.title: Crypto.com valuation hits $20bn after investment from Citadel Securities
top_signals.summary: Crypto.com has reached a valuation of $20 billion following a strategic investment from Citadel Securities. This move highlights the increasing integration of Wall Street market makers into the digital asset and blockchain ecosystem.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Citadel Securities' involvement in Crypto.com's $20 billion valuation is significant because it represents a market maker with deep options-market expertise pricing crypto infrastructure as a core revenue stream rather than a hedged bet.

top_signals.title: FTX to distribute $900M to creditors in fifth payment round7m
top_signals.summary: FTX is set to distribute approximately $900 million to its creditors as part of its fifth payment round. This move is part of the ongoing bankruptcy proceedings to recover and return assets to affected users.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The $900 million FTX creditor distribution matters because it demonstrates that bankruptcy recoveries in crypto can achieve meaningful scale, which gradually reprices counterparty risk assumptions across lending and custody markets.

top_signals.title: World Cup final is already the biggest ever prediction market as Kalshi bets top $1.27 billion—with Spain favored to beat Argentina
top_signals.summary: Prediction markets are seeing massive adoption with the World Cup final, with Kalshi and Polymarket recording over $29 billion in total trading volume. Kalshi specifically has seen bets exceeding $1.27 billion on the final match.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Prediction markets hitting $1.27 billion on a single sporting event with Kalshi and Polymarket's combined $29 billion volume indicates that regulated and offshore venues are simultaneously finding product-market fit in event-derived liquidity, not just price speculation.

top_signals.title: HSBC Approved for Bank of England Digital Securities Sandbox
top_signals.summary: HSBC has become the first applicant approved by the Bank of England to go live in the UK's Digital Securities Sandbox. The bank will utilize its HSBC Orion platform to test the tokenization and settlement of securities.
top_signals.why_it_matters: HSBC's approval in the Bank of England's Digital Securities Sandbox matters because a systemically important bank entering live tokenization testing signals that settlement infrastructure is moving from pilot to production-grade, with regulatory cover.

top_signals.title: SBI Acquires Singaporean Crypto Exchange Coinhako After MAS Approval
top_signals.summary: SBI Holdings has received approval from the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) to acquire a majority stake in the crypto exchange Coinhako. This acquisition is intended to bolster SBI's strategic expansion into stablecoins, on-chain finance, and tokenization.
top_signals.why_it_matters: SBI's MAS-approved acquisition of Coinhako matters because Japanese-Singaporean regulatory arbitrage is being replaced by compliant consolidation, with stablecoin and tokenization licenses as the actual assets being acquired.

deals.summary: SBI Holdings has received approval from the Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) to acquire a majority stake in the crypto exchange Coinhako. This acquisition is intended to bolster SBI's strategic expansion into stablecoins, on-chain finance, and tokenization.
ORANGE JUICE has raised $40 million to establish a permanent capital firm. The firm intends to acquire businesses while implementing a strategic Bitcoin treasury model.

Crypto exchange Bybit has officially launched its services in Indonesia following the acquisition of NOBI. This move allows Bybit to establish a legal presence and expand its user base in the Southeast Asian market.
Polygon Labs has announced its second round of layoffs within a year as the company streamlines operations. This restructuring occurs as the firm works toward finalizing the acquisition of Coinme.

MoonPay has acquired Glide, a crypto infrastructure startup founded by former Robinhood Wallet engineers. The acquisition aims to integrate Glide's cross-chain deposit routing technology into MoonPay's existing platform.
Tether has invested $20 million in the Argentine neobank Ualá. This investment was part of a larger $197 million funding round that brought Ualá's valuation to $3.2 billion.

on_the_radar.title: Ostium Left an Opening for Exploiters and $24m Went Out the Door
on_the_radar.summary: The synthetic trading platform Ostium suffered a security exploit resulting in the loss of approximately $23.75 million. The stolen funds were primarily in the form of USDC stablecoins.

on_the_radar.title: Consensys unknowingly outsourced developer work to North Korean9m
on_the_radar.summary: Consensys discovered that it had unknowingly hired developers linked to North Korea for outsourced work. The company has since taken steps to terminate these relationships and enhance its vetting processes.

on_the_radar.title: OKX Europe Lets Users Convert USDT to MiCA-Compliant USDC
on_the_radar.summary: OKX Europe has introduced a tool allowing users to convert USDT to USDC. This move is a proactive response to the Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) regulation, which imposes restrictions on non-compliant stablecoins within the EU.

on_the_radar.title: Crypto-style derivatives reach AI compute ahead of planned CME and ICE futures: Bernstein
on_the_radar.summary: Bernstein reports that crypto-style perpetuals and prediction markets are currently leading the way in AI compute derivatives. This trend precedes the expected launch of regulated GPU futures from CME and ICE, which are targeted for late 2026.

on_the_radar.title: Weekly Top Stories: Shakeup at Coinbase's Base
on_the_radar.summary: A weekly news summary highlighting organizational changes at Coinbase's Base network and a significant security breach. The report also mentions a freeze on data centers in New York.

on_the_radar.title: UK sentences 2 hackers tied to $115M crypto ransom scheme30m
on_the_radar.summary: Two hackers have been sentenced in the UK for their involvement in a cryptocurrency ransom scheme totaling $115 million. The legal action highlights ongoing efforts by authorities to combat cybercrime and ransomware within the digital asset ecosystem.

on_the_radar.title: MacOS Malware Uses Telegram Session Hijacking to Target Crypto Wallets
on_the_radar.summary: A new macOS malware has been identified that targets cryptocurrency wallets by hijacking Telegram sessions. The malware steals credentials and decrypts wallet databases to compromise user assets.

on_the_radar.title: Ledger unveils hardware-backed Agent Stack to prevent rogue AI transactions
on_the_radar.summary: Ledger has introduced the Agent Stack, a hardware-backed framework designed to secure AI-driven transactions. The system allows users to deploy bots for portfolio management and transaction drafting while preventing rogue AI from executing unauthorized transfers.

worth_a_read.title: Ostium Left an Opening for Exploiters and $24m Went Out the Door
worth_a_read.note: Galaxy's analysis of Ostium's $24 million exploit is worth reading because it examines how perpetual futures DEXs with novel oracle designs create specific attack surfaces that differ materially from lending protocol exploits.

worth_a_read.title: Weekly Top Stories: Shakeup at Coinbase's Base
worth_a_read.note: The Base leadership shakeup coverage merits attention because Coinbase's L2 strategy is a bellwether for how US-listed exchanges navigate the tension between decentralized sequencing narratives and centralized revenue capture.

worth_a_read.title: Mollie doubles down on Europe with €350m expansion plan: ‘Superapp is a convoluted word’
worth_a_read.note: Sifted's interview with Mollie's CEO is relevant because his explicit rejection of the 'superapp' framing for European fintech expansion offers a counter-narrative to the bundling thesis that many Web3 consumer plays rely on.

linkedin_post:
Ken Griffin's shop does not price $20 billion by accident. Citadel Securities taking a strategic position in Crypto.com at that valuation is a market maker with real-time flow data declaring that the exchange infrastructure layer has reached institutional-grade durability. They see the order book. We do not. But we can read what they underwrite.

The same week, HSBC goes live in the Bank of England's tokenization sandbox. SBI gets MAS approval to buy Coinhako for its stablecoin license stack. Kalshi and Polymarket clear $29 billion combined volume. These are not correlated hype cycles. They are separate regulatory and commercial systems converging on the same repricing: crypto as settlement and prediction infrastructure, not as speculative asset class.

What we underwrite a sector on is shifting. The question is no longer whether tokenization happens. It is whether the first-mover advantage in regulated sandboxes like HSBC's Orion deployment compounds into network effects before the technology commoditizes. The test: in twelve months, does the BoE sandbox produce live corporate bond settlement at reduced cost, or does it remain a press release?

If it is the latter, the infrastructure valuations reprice down hard. If it is the former, the Citadel mark starts to look conservative.
